novelty_basis: Searched (2026-10-18) - de Bruijn cycles with distance constraints, universal cycles of Latin squares/quasigroups, Tuscan-2 squares (Etzion, Golomb, Taylor, Adv. Appl. Math. 10 (1989) - a related but different object: n x n arrays, pairs at distance <= 2 at most once across rows), orthogonal de Bruijn sequences. No statement of this characterisation or of these cycles found. Small.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C16.md Theorem 4); the exhaustive Latin-square count and the independent distance-1/2 DFS count agree (EXP-C16-02); awaiting independent skeptic review
statement:
A full-period table is a quasigroup iff in its cycle x_0 ... x_{n^2-1} every ordered pair also occurs exactly once
as (x_i, x_{i+2}); equivalently the windows (x_{i-1}, x_i, x_{i+1}) run once through the n^2 triples
(a, b, b*a) of the Latin square (a universal cycle of the quasigroup).
title: Full-period quasigroups are cycles in which every pair occurs once at distance 1 and once at distance 2
